comments.author: @HoracioME
comments.text:
I want to address the incredible lie that has been spread accusing Argentinians of being racist. To do so, I will give a brief historical overview.

At a time when it was a nearly uninhabited territory, there was a portion of the population of African descent, children of slaves (because the freedom of wombs was declared in 1813 by a government that rose up against Spanish rule but had not yet declared independence, which occurred in 1816). During the war for independence and later the yellow fever epidemic that broke out mainly in the poorest neighborhoods, many of the Black population died.
It should be clarified that even from the beginning of the Spanish viceroyalty, the slave population was not as significant as in Brazil or the USA because in Argentina, economic activity was not linked to large plantations where slave labor was used; such plantations practically did not exist.

Furthermore, since racial segregation never existed, the Black population mixed with the white population, resulting in mulatto children who, in turn, intermarried with whites, thus diluting the original Black population.

The same occurred between whites and Amerindians (Indigenous peoples).
This social characteristic became noticeably more pronounced with the arrival of mass immigration.
When the total population of Argentina—including whites, Blacks, Amerindians, mulattos, mestizos, etc.—was 1 million, 5 million immigrants arrived in the country, mostly from the famine-stricken Europe of the late 19th and early 20th centuries. There were also citizens who had been under the influence of the Ottoman Empire, such as Syrian-Lebanese—five times more than the resident population at that time!

The phenomenon of racial mixing became increasingly pronounced, and given the disproportionate difference, the Black population became even more diluted. That's why it's been proven that a significant percentage of Argentinian citizens have some African ancestry, while others have white ancestry, even though you can't verify this through their features due to the predominance of the latter.
This isn't my own invention; it's all properly documented.

It's ridiculous that the country that opened its doors to any citizen of goodwill who wishes to live on Argentine soil, as stated in the preamble to the National Constitution enacted in 1853, is accused of this infamy, particularly by people from the USA, where until the 1960s there were separate bathrooms for Black and white people, and where even today a white police officer occasionally murders a Black American by abusing their authority. Much less so by Europeans who have plundered and enslaved the African continent, the terrible consequences of which are still visible today.

Has it reached the point of absurdity to question why there are no Black soccer players on the Argentine national team?

Like a journalist from the New York Times did, who probably has no idea where our country is or has never even watched a soccer match in her life. It's unbelievable. For the same reason there aren't any on the national teams of  Mexico, Chile, Paraguay, Bolivia, South Korea, China, or Japan, to name a few examples.

Could it be that while in France Black people living in ghettos face discrimination, when it suits some of them or their children's sporting interests, they are incorporated into national sports teams (Mbappé)? The same thing happens in Spain with Moroccan immigrants and their children (Yamal). 

Pure hypocrisy and cynicism.

I don't know if it's due to immense ignorance, some resentment, or simply joining an absurd campaign that has taken hold on social media.

Or perhaps there's some darker interest behind it.

It's striking that after the famous banner displayed at the World Cup, where Argentinians claimed their legitimate rights over the Malvinas (Falkland) Islands, this campaign grew exponentially.
Or perhaps it has something to do with our ridiculous current president, whom, God willing, we will properly replace next year through our votes in the general elections.
What nation is proud of its president? I'm sure most would answer no, absolutely not.
Most of us aren't either.
To those who might read this, believe me or not, I invite you to read the posts of Black people who, for various reasons, have come to this country and see what they think.
There are several participants in this very forum.
Greetings to the good people who participate in this forum; as for the malicious ones, that's their problem.
